newsitem.title: USA: Plaintiff says US Prudential Ins. settles case.
newsitem.headline: Plaintiff says US Prudential Ins. settles case.

text.p: Prudential Insurance Co of America entered a settlement of a lawsuit filed by a man who claimed the company misrepresented the sale of an insurance policy, the plaintiff's lawyers said.
Terms of the settlement were confidential, attorney Joseph Roda, of Roda & Nast, said in a statement.

Richard Rutt, age 60 who died in July 1996 before the settlement was reached, bought a $100,000 cash value life insurance policy from Prudential in 1990 and cashed in other insurance policies to fund the premiums, Roda said.
Prudential was not immediately available for comment.
The agent told Rutt that his first premium payment would be approximately $1,500 to $2,000 after the fifth year of the plan, Roda said. Rutt filed his case against the company in 1993.
At the end of the second year, however, Rutt received premium notices and the agent told him that he would need to make premium payments $4,800 a year to prevent the policy from lapsing, Roda said.
Prudential paid Rutt's family $100,362 after he died and noted that certain procedures were not followed in the sale of the insurance policy, Roda said.

The family proceeded with the case, since they contend that Prudential acted in bad faith by refusing to honor the promise the agent made or when the company recognized the truth of the claims made by Rutt's wife, Roda said.

Prudential had attempted to offer reinstating a smaller policy that was cashed in to pay for the larger policy and refund the money that was originally paid after an internal investigation in 1993, Roda said.
